annotation_description: Playing Breeding Pool turn 1 provides U/G mana but doesn't advance toward the {1}{B} needed to cast Overlord of the Balemurk's impending cost on turn 2. The fetch land or Overgrown Tomb would have been better first plays to set up the key turn 2 play.

annotation_description: The player is evoking Subtlety (which requires exiling a blue card from hand) and chose to exile Deceit instead of Force of Negation. Deceit is a powerful card that provides both bounce and hand disruption effects, and costs 6 mana making it harder to cast but very impactful. Force of Negation is also strong but is more situational (only counters noncreature spells, and its free cast only works on opponent's turn). However, in this deck that appears to be a graveyard-focused strategy with Overlord of the Balemurk and Persist, keeping Force of Negation is reasonable as protection against opposing interaction. But Deceit can be recurred via Overlord of the Balemurk's ability (returning a non-Avatar creature from graveyard to hand) if it ends up in the graveyard, whereas exiling it removes that option entirely. Force of Negation exiled is less of a loss since it can't be recurred anyway. The player should have exiled Force of Negation to preserve Deceit for potential recursion with Overlord of the Balemurk.

Playing Swamp instead of Polluted Delta is slightly suboptimal. With Thoughtseize in hand wanting to cast it this turn (needing black mana), both lands work. However, Polluted Delta is generally better to play first because: 1) It can fetch a Swamp (or Island) later if needed, but playing it now and cracking it gives the same mana access while thinning the deck. 2) More importantly, keeping the fetchland uncracked preserves future flexibility, but playing Swamp now means the Polluted Delta will be played later when it could have been played turn 1 to fetch. The key consideration is that Psychic Frog wants cards in the graveyard for its exile-three ability, and a cracked fetchland contributes to graveyard count. Also, having a fetchland in play gives shuffle effects and flexibility. Playing Polluted Delta, fetching a Swamp (paying 1 life), and casting Thoughtseize would put a fetchland in the graveyard for Psychic Frog while preserving the basic Swamp for future land drops (basics can't be Wastelanded in formats that have it, though this is Modern). The life cost is minor (1 life for fetch + 2 for Thoughtseize = 3 total vs just 2 for Thoughtseize with Swamp), but graveyard building for Psychic Frog and deck thinning generally favor leading with the fetchland.

Fetching a basic Forest instead of a dual land that produces black mana. The hand contains Overlord of the Balemurk (3BB), Deceit (4UB/UB), and Overgrown Tomb. The player has Breeding Pool (G/U) in play and Overgrown Tomb in hand. Fetching a basic Forest provides only green mana, which is largely redundant. The player needs black mana sources to cast their spells. Fetching Watery Grave (U/B) or Overgrown Tomb from the library would provide access to black mana immediately (paying 2 life) while keeping the Overgrown Tomb in hand as another land drop. With a basic Forest, the player is further from casting their key spells.

Playing Polluted Delta before casting Thoughtseize is a sequencing error. Thoughtseize costs only {B} and the player already has a Swamp untapped. By casting Thoughtseize first, they would see the opponent's hand and gain information that could influence which land to fetch (e.g., whether they need UB for Psychic Frog next turn, or want to sequence differently). Playing the fetch land first and potentially cracking it wastes the opportunity to use that information. Additionally, if they play Polluted Delta and crack it, they pay 1 life unnecessarily before casting Thoughtseize (which also costs 2 life), when they could cast Thoughtseize first with the Swamp, then play and crack the delta afterward with full information.

Casting Thoughtseize before playing Polluted Delta is a sequencing error. By fetching first with Polluted Delta, Qwen3 could find an untapped dual land (like Overgrown Tomb or Watery Grave) to have access to both black mana sources, preserving flexibility. More importantly, playing the land first is free and doesn't cost any resources, while Thoughtseize before land drop means if they want to cast a 2-drop like Psychic Frog this turn, they need to crack Polluted Delta anyway. The correct sequence is: crack Polluted Delta first to get the right land, then cast Thoughtseize with better information about mana availability for the rest of the turn. Additionally, casting Thoughtseize (losing 2 life) before seeing if they even need it (they could deploy Psychic Frog turn 2 instead) is debatable, but the primary issue is not fetching first - fetching first lets you see an additional card from your library which marginally improves your decisions, and ensures you have the right mana configuration.

Qwen3 Vorthos chose to take Overlord of the Balemurk over Deceit with Thoughtseize. Deceit is a 5/5 with powerful ETB effects (hand disruption or bounce) and can be evoked cheaply, making it a versatile and immediate threat. Overlord of the Balemurk at 5 mana is powerful but slower. However, Deceit's evoke cost is only {U/B}{U/B}, meaning the opponent could cast it very soon for its evoke effect (bouncing a permanent or forcing a discard). With the opponent at only 2 lands, the Overlord is further away from being cast. On the other hand, Overlord's impending mode at {1}{B} means it could come down turn 3 as an enchantment that mills and recurs creatures - and the opponent already has Subtlety in the graveyard to potentially recur. This is a close decision and reasonable players could disagree. Taking Deceit might have been slightly better since it's immediately castable via evoke and provides flexible disruption, but taking Overlord (which generates recurring value and can recur the Subtlety from graveyard) is also defensible.

Fetched a second copy of Overgrown Tomb when they already had one in hand, rather than diversifying their mana base. For casting Deceit (which wants UU or BB), having access to Hedge Maze (Forest Island) would provide a second blue source alongside Breeding Pool, enabling the UU mode of Deceit more easily. The duplicate Overgrown Tomb offers less flexibility.

Playing Overgrown Tomb instead of Misty Rainforest is slightly suboptimal. Fetch lands are generally better to play earlier for deck thinning and flexibility - Misty Rainforest could fetch whatever dual land is needed based on the game situation, preserving both Overgrown Tombs for later turns when specific mana is needed.

Casting Deceit for 6 mana when the player only has 3 lands on the battlefield (Breeding Pool, Forest, Overgrown Tomb) and hasn't played a land yet this turn. Even after playing a land (Overgrown Tomb or Misty Rainforest), they'd only have 4 mana available - far short of the 6 needed to cast Deceit. Additionally, casting Deceit without spending UU or BB means neither of its enters-the-battlefield abilities would trigger meaningfully. The player should instead play a land and cast Formidable Speaker, which costs only 3 mana (within budget) and provides a tutor effect by discarding a card.

annotation_description: GPT4om Valley chose to cast Deceit for its full mana cost of {4}{U/B}{U/B} (6 mana), but they only have 3 lands on the battlefield (Breeding Pool, Forest, Overgrown Tomb) and haven't played a land yet this turn. Even with playing one of the two lands in hand (Overgrown Tomb or Misty Rainforest), they would only have 4 mana available. They cannot pay 6 mana this turn. Choosing Evoke for {U/B}{U/B} (2 mana) would have been castable and would provide an ETB effect (either bounce a nonland permanent or force a discard depending on colors spent) before the creature is sacrificed. By choosing the full cost, the spell likely cannot resolve properly or represents a fundamental misunderstanding of available resources. Additionally, even if somehow the full cost could be paid, the Evoke option gives immediate value - the opponent has only 2 tapped lands and an empty board, so bouncing isn't great, but forcing a discard from Qwen3's hand (if BB was spent) could be very valuable given that the opponent likely has threats in hand.

Cast Formidable Speaker before playing a land. While the opponent's lands are tapped reducing risk, proper sequencing would be to play Misty Rainforest first (and potentially crack it) to have 4 mana available after casting the creature, keeping options open. Playing lands before spells is a fundamental sequencing principle.

Casting Endurance before playing a land is a sequencing error. GPT4om Valley has both Overgrown Tomb and Misty Rainforest in hand, and all three lands are tapped. Playing Misty Rainforest first (free land drop) and then cracking it would put a land into play untapped, enabling more mana. More importantly, casting Endurance with all lands tapped means using the evoke cost (exiling a green card), but Endurance costs {1}{G}{G} to hardcast. With only 3 lands all tapped, they can't hardcast it this turn anyway. However, if they play a land first and pass, they'd have 4 mana next turn to hardcast Endurance (keeping it on the battlefield as a 3/4 reach creature) rather than having to evoke it now. The opponent has no graveyard-dependent threats that demand immediate Endurance use - their graveyard contains Thoughtseize, Unearth, Fatal Push, Faithless Looting, and Polluted Delta, but the opponent only has 2 tapped lands and can't flash back Faithless Looting or cast Unearth/Persist targeting anything dangerous right now. Evoking Endurance now to shuffle the opponent's graveyard (denying future Faithless Looting flashback and Unearth) has some value, but losing a 3/4 body is a significant cost when you could just wait a turn to hardcast it.

Playing Overgrown Tomb instead of Misty Rainforest is slightly suboptimal. Misty Rainforest is generally better to play first because: (1) It can fetch any Forest or Island, giving more flexibility later. (2) Sacrificing a fetchland triggers Revolt for potential interactions and puts a card in the graveyard. (3) It keeps the Overgrown Tomb in hand for a future turn where you might want to choose whether to pay 2 life. (4) Most importantly, with Endurance in hand (which costs {1}{G}{G}), playing Misty Rainforest and fetching a Forest would give access to GGG next turn (Forest + Overgrown Tomb + Breeding Pool), making it easier to cast Endurance. Playing Overgrown Tomb now means next turn you'd need to play Misty Rainforest and fetch to get the right colors, which achieves the same thing but with less flexibility this turn. The difference is marginal since all lands are tapped this turn anyway, but fetching now would also enable Revolt for any potential Fatal Push-like interactions and thin the deck.

Forestcycling Generous Ent when they already have Misty Rainforest in hand gives them two land cards in hand with only one land drop per turn. They already have 5 lands on the battlefield. The mana spent on cycling could have been used more productively, and playing Misty Rainforest first to crack it would have been better sequencing regardless.

Casting Endurance in the precombat main phase is suboptimal timing. Endurance has flash, so it could be cast at instant speed during the opponent's turn (e.g., in response to them trying to use their graveyard with Unearth or Faithless Looting flashback). Casting it now in your own main phase gives the opponent full information and the ability to play around it. Additionally, casting Endurance before combat means the opponent sees the 3/4 body before blocks matter, and GPT4om Valley should play the Misty Rainforest from hand first before casting spells to avoid missing the land drop if something goes wrong. The graveyard hate effect targeting the opponent is reasonable since Qwen3 Vorthos has Faithless Looting (flashback), Unearth, and Fatal Push in their graveyard, but the timing could be better.

Underground Mortuary provides B/G mana, colors GPT4om Valley already has abundant access to (2x Overgrown Tomb + Forest for G, 2x Overgrown Tomb for B). Hedge Maze would provide a second blue source (currently only Breeding Pool), which is important for casting cards like Deceit (which needs UU for the bounce mode) or other blue spells they might draw.

GPT4om Valley forestcycled Generous Ent to find a Forest when they already had Misty Rainforest in hand that could fetch a Forest. This wastes a 5/7 reach creature that could have been hard-cast next turn with 6 mana (after playing and cracking Misty Rainforest). Instead they end up with 7 lands and no threats in hand.

Playing Hedge Maze (which enters tapped) instead of Misty Rainforest (which can immediately crack for an untapped land) means GPT4om Valley has less mana available this turn. Misty Rainforest would provide an untapped land immediately, giving access to more mana for potential plays or responses. Hedge Maze enters tapped and provides no mana this turn. While the surveil 1 from Hedge Maze has some value, the tempo loss of playing a tapped land over a fetchland is suboptimal, especially when facing an opponent's Psychic Frog that could grow and threaten. Additionally, saving the Hedge Maze for a later turn when tempo matters less would have been better sequencing.

Chump-blocking with Psychic Frog trades away a key threat that generates card advantage (draws on combat damage, grows with discards) for minimal value. The Frog dies without killing anything since Endurance is 3/4. At 15 life, taking the combat damage is affordable.

Formidable Speaker's activated ability '{1}, {T}: Untap another target permanent' was used to untap Ragavan, Nimble Pilferer — an opponent's creature. This gives the opponent's Ragavan the ability to block when it otherwise would have been tapped, or simply provides no benefit to GPT4om Valley. Untapping an opponent's creature is actively detrimental. GPT4om Valley should have untapped one of their own tapped lands (like Underground Mortuary which was tapped) to generate additional mana, or simply untapped one of their own permanents for value.

Attacking Ragavan (2/1) into an untapped Endurance (3/4) risks losing Ragavan for free, as Endurance survives the block. The opponent has no reason not to block. Meanwhile, Psychic Frog could have been pumped and given flying (by discarding a card and exiling 3 graveyard cards) to fly over Endurance for damage + card draw, though this would compromise the graveyard count needed for Abhorrent Oculus.

GPT4om Valley cast Shardless Agent before playing Misty Rainforest from hand. Playing the land first is strictly better sequencing: it ensures the land drop isn't missed, and more importantly, sacrificing Misty Rainforest before casting Shardless Agent would enable Revolt for any Fatal Push that might be cascaded into (though that's not in their deck). Additionally, cracking a fetchland before cascade lets you shuffle away unwanted top cards and thin the deck slightly, marginally improving cascade hits. There's also the consideration that if Shardless Agent cascades into something that requires mana, having an extra land in play could matter. Playing land before spells is a fundamental sequencing principle.

Fetching a basic Island when Watery Grave would provide both U and B flexibility. With cards like Overlord of the Balemurk ({3}{B}{B}) in the graveyard and potential Persist targets, having dual-color access could matter. The player is light on blue sources but already has reasonable black access, so this is somewhat defensible.

Should play Polluted Delta before casting any spells to maximize available mana. With 3 mana available after fetching, Qwen3 could cast Abhorrent Oculus (a 5/5 flyer for {2}{U}, exiling 6 of 8 graveyard cards), which is likely the strongest available play this turn.

Should play Polluted Delta before making any Psychic Frog activation decisions. Playing the land first and fetching gives access to additional mana for post-combat plays like Persist or Bitter Triumph, and the land drop is free with no downside to playing it first.

Declined to crack Polluted Delta in response to Deceit on the stack. Cracking it would fetch an untapped land (giving more mana availability), thin the deck, and add another card to the graveyard (useful for Psychic Frog's flying ability and general graveyard synergies). There's no downside to fetching now versus later, and if Deceit's bounce or discard mode disrupts plans, having the land already in play is strictly better.

With opponent's board tapped out and two ground blockers (Formidable Speaker 2/4, Endurance 3/4) preventing profitable attacks, Qwen3 Vorthos could have discarded a card to pump Psychic Frog and exiled 3 graveyard cards to give it flying, enabling an unblockable 2-damage attack that draws a card. They have 9 graveyard cards and would still retain 6 for Abhorrent Oculus.

Psychic Frog could have been pumped by discarding a card and given flying (exile 3 cards from graveyard) to attack for 2+ damage through the air and draw a card, since opponent's all lands are tapped and can't interact. With 10 cards in graveyard, flying is available. Discarding Persist (can't be cast this turn anyway with all lands tapped) to pump Frog, then giving it flying for a 2/3 flying attacker that draws on hit seems like good value.

Fetching basic Island when the hand contains Bitter Triumph and Persist (both requiring {1}{B}) with only one black source (Swamp). A second black source would allow casting both black spells or having redundancy if Swamp gets disrupted. The Island only adds blue mana which Steam Vents already provides.

Psychic Frog can attack into a completely tapped-out board with no blockers available. The combat damage trigger draws a card, which is pure value. Additionally, Qwen3 could discard a Persist to pump Frog to 2/3, dealing more damage and drawing a card. At 7 life with only 3 cards in hand, the card draw is critically important.

annotation_description: Qwen3 Vorthos chose to Persist back Psychic Frog (a 1/2 that becomes 0/1 with the -1/-1 counter) instead of Abhorrent Oculus (a 5/5 flyer that becomes 4/4 with the counter and generates manifest dread tokens every opponent's upkeep). The graveyard has 13 cards, well more than the 6 needed for Oculus's additional cost (which only applies when casting, not when put onto the battlefield via Persist). At 7 life facing an opponent with Formidable Speaker and Endurance (both tapped), Abhorrent Oculus as a 4/4 flyer would be a massive threat that dominates the board and generates card advantage every turn. Psychic Frog as a 0/1 is nearly useless — it needs discard fuel to grow and the hand is now empty after casting Persist.

annotation_description: Formidable Speaker's activated ability ({1}, {T}: Untap another target permanent) was used to target Deceit, which is in the graveyard, not on the battlefield. This appears to be a misunderstanding of the board state - Deceit is listed in the graveyard, not as a permanent on the battlefield. The player wasted Formidable Speaker's tap ability (preventing it from attacking) to untap something that likely doesn't exist as a valid target. Meanwhile, with the opponent at 7 life and having creatures that could attack, tapping Formidable Speaker for no meaningful benefit is costly. The player should have either attacked with Formidable Speaker or used the untap ability on one of their own tapped lands to have mana available.

annotation_description: Generous Ent costs 6 mana and is slow. Endurance (3 mana, flash, reach) would be cheaper to deploy, can block flying Frogs, and critically its ETB can shuffle the opponent's graveyard - disrupting Psychic Frog's ability to exile cards for flying. Subtlety could also be evoked for free to counter a future creature spell. With 0 cards in hand and needing efficient plays, the expensive Ent is suboptimal.

Only attacking with Deceit (5/5) when attacking with all three creatures (Deceit 5/5, Endurance 3/4, Shardless Agent 2/2 = 10 power) against an opponent at 7 life would guarantee more damage gets through. The opponent only has two Psychic Frogs (1/2) to block with, meaning they can only nullify two attackers, and the third always gets through. Attacking all guarantees at least 2 damage and likely trades away the opponent's Psychic Frogs.

At 7 life facing lethal (10 damage from Shardless Agent 2/2 + Deceit 5/5 + Endurance 3/4), Qwen3 chose to block Shardless Agent (the smallest attacker) with a Psychic Frog. With two Frogs available as blockers, the optimal assignment is to block the two largest creatures (Deceit and Endurance), taking only 2 damage from Shardless Agent and surviving at 5 life. By blocking Shardless Agent instead, the best remaining assignment has the other Frog on Deceit, taking 3 from Endurance and surviving at 4 life - one unnecessary life point lost.
